findings.impact: An implementation could silently weaken accepted test behavior by modifying an omitted helper, fixture, or configuration file.
findings.text: The child-repository section says to resolve “test-scoped paths” and protect their entries, but does not define how that scope is derived or require it to include every child path changed by the accepted test checkpoint. The existing superproject rule at plugins/zzzops/zzzops/engine/verbs.py:frozen_paths freezes every changed path since the pre-test work/base, not just files identified as tests. An implementation could choose files by test name or worker declaration, omit a test fixture/helper/config changed during test authoring, and then alter it in the child implementation while the listed test files remain equal; accepted behavior can be weakened without detection. Specify a deterministic child baseline and derive the protected union from all changed child entries through the accepted test checkpoint (including additions, removals, renames and non-test-named helpers), retain prior accepted paths on retries, and fail closed when provenance cannot establish the full scope. Add a real child-repository regression in which an accepted test calls a changed helper and modifying or deleting only that helper is rejected. Impact: implementers could otherwise change accepted test behavior without review, violating the stated preservation guarantee. Material: true.

output.summary: Child checkpoint protection needs a complete, deterministic protected-path scope; otherwise a helper changed with accepted tests can be omitted and silently weakened.

responses.adversary_design:1:1: fixed: Specify the pre-test child gitlink baseline and full changed-entry union through accepted checkpoints, including blocked/retry history, explicit absent entries and fail-closed provenance; require helper-only real-child regression tests.
responses.review_design:1:1: fixed: Keep false route pending while scaffold work/findings or a live lease require resolution, require reviewed exact retained checkpoint or separately reviewed removal, and cover waiver and unresolved finding cases.
responses.review_design:1:2: fixed: Make the boolean and producer identity explicit fingerprinted inputs to adversarial challenge, design filter and owner approval context, and require stale-gate tests with unchanged prose summaries.

output.summary: The revised design fails closed on route changes, fingerprints the route into design challenge and approval, and protects every changed child path and prior retry scope using verifiable Git checkpoint provenance. It preserves the owner-selected optional scaffold route, independently reviewed test protection, and separate migration-defect scope.

Both independent reviews found three material issues that reopen design: child checkpoint scope must include all changed test-helper paths; false-route transitions must not bypass unresolved scaffold findings; and route changes must stale filter and approval context. No non-material notes require verdicts.

findings.impact: An agent can bypass a material scaffold-review finding and carry unreviewed scaffold behavior into implementation.
findings.text: Specify a fail-closed true-to-false transition when scaffold work or its review has open material findings. Merely keeping those findings visible does not prevent a derived skip from making review_scaffold optional and letting test_design run with the existing scaffold commits still in the work branch. Require resolution or explicit waiver, or remove/revert the affected scaffold checkpoint through a reviewed transition before the false route can proceed; cover the case with a real workflow test.

findings.impact: A changed route can proceed without the independent challenge or approval context associated with the current decision.
findings.text: Make the route decision an explicit fingerprinted input to the design filter and its review/approval context, not just to the conditional nodes. The existing filter reads review_design.summary, and approve_design reads filter_design.summary; changing scaffold_needed while summaries remain equal need not stale either record, so the filter/adversarial challenge and owner approval can remain current for the previous route. Specify re-review and approval behavior for a changed decision, and test a re-review that flips the boolean while leaving summaries unchanged.

not: A ceremony framework: every mechanism must prevent a real failure worth its cost.
A second source of truth beside Git.
An engine that invents human decisions or acts without authority.
A deploy, CI or release-publishing tool: its release support is a branching strategy.
Inherently opinionated: it ships an opinionated default graph, but every opinion (graph, lenses, prompts, policy) can be customised by the project.
principles: Git is the store; state is visible and repairable by hand.
A small engine; the graph, prompts and policy belong to the project.
Human authority is explicit: approvals may be delegated, but decisions with big consequences go to the owner, batched.
Reviews are independent, and a finding must matter.

Guard against drift at both levels: from what a goal asked for, and from the project's original intent. A goal that departs from the project's intent is flagged when it is added, and the owner either changes the goal or amends the intent.
Prefer deleting to adding; keep prompts distilled.
intent.purpose: Let coding agents carry long-running repository work through durable, reviewable goals, so a developer can stop supervising without losing progress, priorities or control.
intent.serves: Developers who delegate project work to coding agents, and the agents doing it.

output.summary: The revised design closes both routing findings with fail-closed transitions and fingerprinted review gates.

spec:
Improve the shipped default ZzzOps DAG so test authors can work against the real interfaces and wiring they need before the behavior is implemented, without forcing this step on goals that already have suitable interfaces.

Context: Project Base G12 exposed substantial friction in test design because the approved behavior required runtime-config, deployment, player configuration and bootstrap interfaces that did not exist. Tests either had to guess production APIs, exercise an unrelated helper rather than real composition, or send the design back through approval for routine testability details. The goal also spans package repositories and a superproject with Git submodules; test checkpoints must not freeze a package gitlink prematurely and prevent the implementation from updating it.

Acceptance criteria:
- Design and add an optional, appropriately reviewed contract/scaffold stage before test authoring in the shipped default DAG. Where useful, it establishes the minimal real interfaces, composition/wiring or test seams required to write meaningful tests; goals with existing interfaces should avoid unnecessary work and ceremony.
- Clearly define the boundary between contract/scaffold work and implementing the behavior under test. Tests must still independently verify real behavior, and implementation must not be able to weaken accepted tests unnoticed. Allow routine internal test seam choices without unnecessary owner approval while preserving owner decisions on externally consequential contracts.
- Support work that spans packages and Git submodules: preserve reviewable changes in their owning repositories and ensure the superproject's checkpoint/protection rules permit updating gitlinks when package implementations change, without silently weakening test protection.
- Check and document how existing repositories and in-flight goals adopt the changed default DAG, including the expected treatment of history, accepted work, findings, approvals, checkpoint/test protections, leases and policy review. Exercise migration behavior with realistic local fixtures and report failures. If migration does not work properly, address its repair in a separate goal; do not expand this goal to fix unrelated migration defects.
- Test the resulting graph and migration using the real engine and workflow templates. Evaluate whether the added node actually reduces rework and remains optional for simple goals; do not introduce a mandatory ceremony stage.

The project intent prioritizes a small engine and configurable, independently reviewed workflows. Prefer changes in the shipped workflow/prompts over engine changes where feasible; retain compatibility and avoid unrelated workflow redesign. Do not deploy or publish changes without authorization.
title: Add optional pre-test contract scaffolding to the default DAG
